subject: Live Agent Feed delay — action items and short-term mitigations
messages:
From: Rachel Lopez <rachel.lopez@finpay.com>

Cc: FinPay Ops <ops@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live agent feed showing 2-8s gaps — urgent

Hi Aisha,

We started seeing increased latency in the live agent feed this morning — customers on our support chat are seeing 2–8 second gaps during streaming responses between tokens. It started around 07:50 PT and affects ~30% of active sessions on us-west-2. Attachments: screenshot of the client timeline and packet capture.

This is impacting our SLA-backed customers; we’ve already had two escalations into our support queue. Can you advise immediate mitigations we can apply from our side, and whether this is something you’re seeing platform-side?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Lopez

Subject: Re: Live agent feed showing 2-8s gaps — urgent

Hi Rachel — thanks for the heads up and for the screenshots/pcap. We're opening a dedicated incident room and triaging now. Quick answers + immediate customer-side mitigations below: 

What we’re doing (platform):
- Triage the us-west-2 serving pool for streaming backpressure and kernel queueing.
- Check for KV cache hot-shard behavior and recent rollout changes.

Short-term actions you can take (customer):
- If you can, temporarily switch to the non-streaming (poll-based) endpoint for high-SLA widgets until we confirm stabilization (this prevents UI gaps while slightly increasing perceived latency).
- Reduce client-side max_chunk_size to 256 tokens and enable per-request keep_alive=10s to discourage connection churn.
- If you have request-level retry logic, add exponential jitter (start at 200ms) rather than immediate reconnects; aggressive reconnects can amplify backpressure.

I’ll keep you updated — Marissa is on the triage and will follow with technical findings in about 60–90 minutes. If you want, we can stand up a 15m sync in 20 minutes.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Head of Customer Reliability (EMEA & US Customers)

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:05:42 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live agent feed showing 2-8s gaps — urgent

Quick tech summary from triage (what we found):
- Root cause signal: a Kv-cache hotkey pattern combined with a subtle scheduling regression in the streaming runtime that surfaced under bursty short-request traffic. This caused intermittent token dispatch delays ~80–300ms per token that accumulated into the 2–8s gaps you observed.
- Trigger: a config flip deployed to a small subset of us-west-2 edge shards this morning to optimize batching; the change unintentionally increased contention on the prefix cache for short-conversation workloads.

Immediate platform mitigations we applied (done at 10:48 PT):
- Reverted the batching-affinity change on affected edge shards (rollback id: rbk-20260519-01).
- Floated an emergency hotfix to reduce the streaming runtime's scheduling quantum from 12ms -> 6ms (hotfix id: hf-20260519-02).
- Enabled a transient routing rule to shift 25% of traffic from affected shards to warm spare nodes with a different kernel profile.

Recommended short-term customer steps (what you can do now):
1) If you can accept slightly higher p99 server latency but no token gaps: switch to the non-chunked streaming mode (disable client-side chunk buffering) for critical sessions — this prevents client replay issues.
2) Set header X-Redwood-Prefer-Fallback: fast-token to route to the lower-batched variant (temporary knob).
3) Reduce your client-side token chunk window to 128–256 tokens and add a 100–300ms read timeout before initiating reconnect.

Attachments uploaded: stream-logs-20260519.zip (server logs from the affected shards), device-screenshots.png (customer timeline).

Planned next steps:
- Monitor stabilization metrics for 4h; if gaps persist we will temporarily divert 50% traffic to dedicated warm nodes and keep you posted.
- Full postmortem and permanent fix prioritized on the infra backlog with ETA 72 hours.

Let me know if you want that 15m stand-up; we can invite your ops lead and walk through the rollback and knobs.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole

Rachel — summary and next steps: 

Summary:
- Cause: workload-specific cache contention combined with a recent batching-affinity config change on a subset of us-west-2 shards.
- Impact: intermittent token gaps (2–8s) for ~30% sessions; degraded UX but not loss of data.
- Immediate fixes: rollback + scheduling quantum hotfix + partial traffic reroute (completed by 10:51 PT).

What we did for FinPay:
- Confirmed your tenant traffic entered the reroute window and saw error-rate/stream-gap metrics improve within 18 minutes post-rollback.
- Uploaded logs and a short analysis to: https://redwood.app/drive/incident-20260519 (shared with your ops team).

Customer-ready mitigations we recommend for the next 24–72 hours:
- Apply the X-Redwood-Prefer-Fallback header on mission-critical sessions for immediate smoothing.
- Temporarily shift chat widgets to poll-based fallback for the highest SLA corridors (we can help toggle this).
- Plan to accept a p99 increase if you prefer to avoid token gaps while we push a permanent fix.

Post-incident follow-up plan:
- War room recap (internal): Wed 2026-05-20 09:00 PT.
- Customer postmortem call (with FinPay): Thu 2026-05-21 10:00 PT — agenda: root cause, timeline, permanent remediation plan, and compensation/credits if applicable.
- Engineering owner: marissa_cole; PM liaison: evelyn_hart.

If FinPay wants an early heads-up once the permanent patch lands (ETA ~72h), we'll email you and offer a coordinated low-risk rollout window. Please reply with which mitigation options you'd like us to enable for your tenant tonight (prefer: "fallback-header", "poll-mode", or "wait-for-patch").

Appreciate the quick reporting — we'll keep this channel updated until the postmortem.

Best,
